paragraphs.text: The patient reports experiencing a major depressive episode, characterized by persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest in activities, and significant weight loss. The patient also mentions difficulty sleeping, waking up at 4 AM and being unable to return to sleep, resulting in approximately five hours of sleep per night. Appetite has been poor, leading to a ten-pound weight loss. The patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicide, stating that while they sometimes wish they would not wake up, they do not have any plans or intentions to harm themselves.
paragraphs.evidence: I have been feeling really down for about three 3 months, since I lost my job in July. I cry almost every day and I do not enjoy anything anymore. I wake up at four 4 in the morning and cannot get back to sleep, so maybe five 5 hours a night. My appetite is bad and I lost about ten 10 pounds. Sometimes I wish I would not wake up, but I do not want to kill myself and I have no plan.

paragraphs.text: The provider plans to initiate sertraline at a dose of fifty milligrams daily. The provider will see the patient again in two weeks. No sleeping pills or benzodiazepines will be prescribed at this time. Side effects such as nausea and headache were discussed, and the alternative of therapy alone was also considered. The patient agrees to try the sertraline.
